items.q: In the middle ear diagram, which structure forms the primary acoustic impedance matching mechanism between airborne sound and cochlear fluid?
o: Area ratio of tympanic membrane to stapes footplate
Contraction of the tensor tympani muscle
items.exp: The middle ear overcomes the high acoustic impedance of cochlear fluid predominantly via the areal ratio of the tympanic membrane (effective area ~55 mm²) to the stapes footplate (~3.2 mm²), which provides a roughly 17:1 mechanical advantage, boosted further by a 1.3:1 ossicular lever ratio to achieve an overall 20-fold sound pressure amplification.
r: Correct. The areal ratio of tympanic membrane to stapes footplate accounts for most impedance matching.
Incorrect. Malleus mass does not drive the primary pressure amplification.
Incorrect. Tensor tympani dampens sound rather than amplifying it.
Incorrect. Mastoid antrum is an air reservoir, not an acoustic lever.
items.kp: Impedance matching is driven by the ~17:1 area ratio between tympanic membrane and stapes footplate.
